Name: Cheerful Pixels - In Game Art Creator
Author: CosmicSweetpea
Description:
[left][center][left][b]Cheerful Pixels[/b]
[/left]
[left]Cheerful Pixels lets you draw pixel art directly inside Stardew Valley. Cheerful Pixels is intentionally a small, playful art studio, designed to be simple, welcoming, and fun to experiment with.[/left]
[left][/left]
[left]Find Aura Rose in the Mountains and left click her to enter the studio. From there, you can paint, experiment with expressive brushes, preview repeating patterns, and export your artwork as transparent PNG files..[/left]
[left][b]
WHAT IT DOES[/b]
[list]
[*]Paint pixel art directly inside the game[/*]
[*]Choose from several canvas sizes[/*]
[*]Use watercolor, soft brush, ink, dry brush, chalk, texture brush, and more[/*]
[*]Paint with one, two, or three colors at once with the watercolor brush[/*]
[*]Create gradients, shapes, outlines, dithering, and recolors[]Blend, smudge, erase, lift color, and use an eyedropper[/*]
[*]Preview repeating patterns while you work[/*]
[*]Check for and repair visible pattern seams[/*]
[*]View artwork at its actual pixel size[/*]
[*]Export transparent PNG file[/*]
[*]Export enlarged versions for easier sharing[/*]
[*]Open your export folder directly from the studio[/*]
[*]The watercolor brush includes several different painting styles and can work with up to three colors at once, allowing you to create more varied and organic color transitions.[/*]
[/list]
[b]EXPORTING YOUR ARTWORK[/b]
[list]
[*]Click the large Export Studio button near the bottom of the tool list.[/*]
[*]Export your artwork as a transparent PNG[/*]
[*]Choose from different export sizes[/*]
[*]Add optional padding around your artwork[/*]
[*]Export enlarged versions for previews and sharing[/*]
[*]Use Open Export Folder to locate your finished files[/*]
[*]Your artwork will be saved inside the mod’s Exports folder.[/*]
[/list]
[b]WHERE THIS IDEA BEGAN[/b]
The idea behind Cheerful Pixels goes back a long way. For years, much of my work has centered on bridging the gap between traditional and digital art, finding ways to preserve the movement, texture, irregularity, and physical character of real materials inside digital creative tools. In 2017, I created a collection of realistic watercolor brushes for Photoshop, which Adobe later purchased a commercial license for. Those brushes were created from real painted marks. I painted hundreds of individual brushstrokes by hand, scanned them, carefully cleaned and isolated each one, and then went through the long, painstaking process of transforming them into responsive digital tools. I have continued developing realistic brushes and creative tools using that same philosophy. The earliest version of Cheerful Pixels emerged from that idea. It is a continuation of the work I have already been doing for years, bringing together my experience as a traditional artist and texture designer with my love of creating accessible creative tools. This project has been living in the back of my mind for a very long time. Between raising four children, creating artwork, and everything else life brings, I simply needed the time and the right environment to finally begin building it. I did not want to make a complicated creative program. I wanted to create something warm, encouraging, and genuinely fun to open, a place that gives people permission to experiment without worrying about whether the result is good enough.

[b]THE FUTURE OF CHEERFUL PIXELS[/b]
This is only the beginning of a project I would love to continue expanding over time. Future updates may include additional tools, brushes, studio features, export options, and more ways to use your artwork both inside and outside the game. For now, I hope Cheerful Pixels gives you a peaceful little place to create, play, and remember that every piece of artwork begins with one tiny mark.
[/left]
[left]Or, in this case, one cheerful little pixel. 🌹[/left]
[/center]
